## Genuine Child

A raw TeX block must start at the CONTAINING BLOCK's content column (Session 189).
Inside a list item that column is the item's, not the line's, so the macro below really
is at its block's column 0 and quarto really does render the heading. Requiring a literal
column 0 deletes it — Session 184 measured exactly that and rejected the change.

- a list item
  its continuation

# Residual Phantom — Inline TeX

At TOP level the content column is 0, so an indented macro is ordinary paragraph text and
the line below it is that paragraph's continuation. This was a disclosed phantom from
Session 184 until Session 189; it is kept as a control and must stay prose.

   \clearpage
# Not A Heading — Indented Macro At Top Level

A class-A raw-TeX macro is INDENT-INSENSITIVE (Session 190). It interrupts an open paragraph
by making pandoc's `inlineCommand'` fail, which happens at the INLINE level where no column
rule exists — so the heading below it is real at EVERY indent, and the ` {0,3}` cap this row
used to carry deleted it. Measured over the full 0-8 sweep plus three tab spellings.

This paragraph is still open.
    \maketitle
# Below An Indented Class A Macro

The class-B control at the SAME indent must stay prose, and it is what separates "the cap is
wrong for class A" from "the cap is wrong for this file's raw TeX". Class B is block only
where no paragraph is open, so against this one it is inline at every indent 0-7.

This paragraph is still open too.
    \clearpage
# Not A Heading — Indented Class B Macro

A class-A macro also OPENS A FRESH BLOCK, so the line below it starts a new paragraph and a
SETEXT underline can claim it (Session 191). `opensFreshBlock` tested the HTML opener ahead of
its `paragraphOpen` bail but reached the raw-TeX rows only behind it, so this heading was not
mis-levelled — it was absent. 216 of them on Session 190's own container corpus alone.

This paragraph is still open as well.
\maketitle
Setext Below A Class A Macro
===

The class-B control at the same place must stay prose, and it is what decides the change.
Class B is a block only where NO paragraph is open, so against this one it is inline: the
paragraph runs on for three lines, pandoc's setext rule claims exactly ONE line, and quarto
renders no heading at all.

This paragraph is still open yet again.
